name: Pyaaz Kachori
subtitle: Flaky fried pastry with a spiced onion filling, from the sweet shops of Jodhpur

ingredients.note: for the moyan; use oil to keep it vegan

prepNotes: Flakiness comes from moyan — fat rubbed into the flour before any water. When you squeeze a fistful and it holds its shape, you have enough.
Fry low and slow. Hot oil puffs the outside and leaves the inside raw, and the kachori collapses as it cools.

steps.text: Rub the ghee into the flour with salt until it holds together when squeezed, then add water a little at a time to make a firm dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Fry the cumin, fennel, nigella and asafoetida, add the onion and cook until soft and just golden, not brown.
Add the besan and the powdered spices and cook 4-5 minutes until dry and crumbly. Add amchur, cool completely.
steps.tip: The filling must be dry, or the kachori will burst in the oil.

steps.text: Roll small dough balls into cups, fill, gather and seal, then flatten very gently to about 1cm.
Fry in oil kept at a low 130-140C for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until pale gold and covered in blisters.
steps.tip: If they brown in under five minutes the oil is far too hot.

steps.text: Drain on a rack. Serve warm with tamarind and coriander chutneys.

storage: Keeps 2 days in an airtight tin at room temperature. Refresh in a hot oven for 5 minutes; do not microwave or they go soft.
